findings.reason: the parameterisation must be settled (distinct parameter names per scope, or a helper that returns a unique key) before either §24 node is implemented, or the scoped-run claims are silently mis-scoped.
findings.text: §24 builds the new exclusion helper "through `build_path_prefix_filter` with a `negated` flag", but `build_path_prefix_filter` returns its parameters under the hard-coded key `prefixes` (line 298 returns `{"prefixes": list(prefixes)}`), and §24 in the same change moves the five path claims in imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:484,540,597,715,795 off `render_path_prefix_clause(..., "root_filter")` onto that same helper for their `--root` scope; a claim that must both scope and exclude then binds two different lists to one `$prefixes`, so the scope predicate and its negation read the wrong list

findings.reason: the interface budget for the week is 0 public_definitions, so the section must account for the added surface in its own text (what it folds into the owner, or why the helper is unavoidable).
findings.text: §24 states "The section adds that one public helper and no other", adding one public definition to `imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py` and widening the public `build_path_prefix_filter` signature with a `negated` flag, but names no public definition it retires or merges and does not state why none can be

findings.reason: §14 is a cumulative landing record whose landed nodes are named in-line ("The seed fix landed on 2026-10-06", "the paths node … and the code-reset node … landed"), so the residual nodes are recoverable without a design change; the finding is a legibility risk, not a defect that alters the plan.
findings.text: §14 carries `data-status="implementable"` and its code-half prose reads as prospective ("the node adds one helper beside the renderer … that returns the clause and its parameters together"), yet every mechanism it describes is already present at the review base `fc0d90ca2`: `build_path_prefix_filter` (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:282) with exactly that "clause and its parameters together / empty clause and no parameters" contract, its use at ten sites in imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:132,304,399,485,580,620,644,674,707,734 and imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:566, `reset_to_status(..., path_prefixes=...)` (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:66) with the `source_filter` OR-clause (reset.py:102-103), `create_nodes(..., create_only=...)` with the `ON CREATE SET` form (imas_codex/graph/client.py:612-690), `seed_missing_roots`/`create_child_paths` already gone, and the `jt-60sa.yaml` `discovery_roots` already replacing `/analysis/src` with its eleven seeded subdirectories and moving `ofmcauto` to `/analysis/src/OFMC/ofmcauto` (imas_codex/config/facilities/jt-60sa.yaml:140-150) — so an implementer reading §14's list of nodes literally would rebuild landed code and can only distinguish the residual work (the scoped code run, the root-restore, the sensor-order receipt) from the landed work by diffing the tree

findings.reason: an undercounted census invites an implementer to stop at the named fifteen and leave `has_pending_scan_work`/`has_pending_link_work` (graph_ops.py:566,726) unscoped, so a scoped run stays alive on rows outside its named trees — exactly the failure §24 exists to prevent.
findings.text: §24 estimates the exclusion helper's reach at "about fifteen sites in all" but the claims and phase-liveness predicates it must cover number about twenty-two: on the paths side the five path claims plus `has_pending_work` and the five `_has_pending_*_work` helpers (imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:197,265,282,301,318,338 and claims at 465,521,579,688,767), and on the code side the four claims plus six has-work predicates in imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py (claims 95,277,367,457; predicates 566,611,636,660,692,726) and the ingest claim in imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:564

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §24's new facility-aware exclusion helper returns its Cypher parameters under the same fixed key `prefixes` that `build_path_prefix_filter` already hard-codes for `--root` scope, so one query carrying both scopes cannot bind them apart; the interface is not in fact smaller than what it hides, because it leaks a shared parameter namespace across two callers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan consolidates rather than forks: §8 removes five SLURM node-discovery copies onto `resolve_service_url`, §10 deletes the graph client's SLURM duplicate, §15 routes vector-index DDL through `GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes`, §14 retires `seed_missing_roots` and deletes `create_child_paths`, and §24 names one owner (`get_exclusion_config_for_facility`) and one renderer (`build_path_prefix_filter`) rather than re-implementing them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §24 adds one new public helper in imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py and adds a `negated` parameter to the existing public `build_path_prefix_filter` without naming, in its own text, a public definition it retires or merges, and without stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the machinery it extends by name and file (`build_path_prefix_filter`, `render_path_prefix_clause`, `get_exclusion_config_for_facility`, `GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes`, `resolve_service_url`) rather than adding a parallel mechanism; §24 extends `build_path_prefix_filter` (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:282) instead of forking it, and §14's prose describes extending `reset_to_status` (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:66) and `GraphClient.create_nodes` (imas_codex/graph/client.py:605) rather than new subsystems.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the exclusion helper §24 adds is not a bare forwarder: it resolves `get_exclusion_config_for_facility(facility).path_prefixes` (imas_codex/config/discovery_config.py:506) into a negated predicate for ~15–22 call sites, and the plan states why the sites cannot each restate the policy and why `build_path_prefix_filter` is extended (a `negated` flag) rather than duplicated.
